title: [YouPass Collect] - European automobile survey results analysis
prompt: The bar charts display the results from a 2009 survey regarding people’s automobile in a European country. Units are measured in percentage.
Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The two bar charts illustrate the findings of a 2009 survey conducted in a European country, examining how frequently people replace their vehicles and what type of car they tend to purchase.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the data reveals that the majority of car owners in this country tend to keep their vehicles for extended periods rather than replacing them frequently. With regard to car purchases, second-hand vehicles were overwhelmingly the most preferred choice.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding car replacement habits, only a negligible proportion of respondents changed their car on a very frequent basis, with those doing so every year accounting for just 1%, while those replacing it every two years made up 5%. A considerably larger share, at 37%, upgraded their vehicle every three to four years. The single largest group, however, consisted of those who kept their car for five years or more, representing just over half of all respondents at 52%. Meanwhile, those who stated they never changed their car and those who owned no vehicle at all each accounted for a minor share, at 3% and 2%, respectively.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Turning to car purchasing preferences, second-hand vehicles dominated the survey results, with 68% of respondents indicating they typically opt for pre-owned cars. In contrast, 25% of respondents preferred to buy new cars. Those who reported purchasing either new or second-hand depending on the situation constituted a modest 10%, while the proportion who did not own a car mirrored the figure seen in the first chart, at 2%.
